en: be very grateful; be very thankful

examples.en: I thought I'd be more than grateful just to be given an interview.

examples.ko: 표를 구해 주신 것만 해도 감지덕지인데 밥까지 사 주시다니요.
examples.en: I'm already so grateful that you got me a ticket, and now you're even buying me a meal!
I'm just thankful to get my pay on time.

examples.ko: 이렇게 좋은 방을 싸게 빌려주시니 감지덕지할 따름이에요.
examples.en: You're renting me such a nice room so cheaply, I can't thank you enough.

examples.ko: 친구가 차로 데려다 주겠다고 해서 감지덕지했어요.
examples.en: My friend offered to drive me there, and I was really grateful.
Wouldn't you be happy with a result like that?

explain: 기대가 크지 않았는데 그것만으로도 고맙고 만족스럽다는 느낌이에요. 그래서 '~만 해도 감지덕지', '~면 감지덕지'처럼 자주 말해요. 그냥 '고맙다'보다 '이 정도도 과분하다'는 뉘앙스가 있어요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling that you expected little, so even this much is more than enough. People often say '~만 해도 감지덕지' or '~면 감지덕지'. Compared with a plain '고맙다', it implies 'even this is more than I deserve'.

en: feel unsatisfied and want more; tease

examples.en: They gave me just a tiny taste, so it only makes me crave more.

examples.ko: 드라마가 일주일에 한 편만 나와서 감질났어요.
examples.en: The drama only airs one episode a week, so it left me wanting more.

examples.ko: 감질나게 조금씩 말하지 말고 다 이야기해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't tease me by telling it bit by bit. Tell me everything.

examples.ko: 샘플만 먹어 보니까 더 감질나는 거 있죠?
examples.en: Having tried only the sample, I'm craving more, you know?

examples.ko: 빵을 한 입만 먹었더니 감질나서 더 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: I only had one bite of the bread, so I'm left wanting more.
They told me to eat only a little, so it's unsatisfying, but I'll hold back.

explain: 조금만 맛보거나 조금만 해서 성에 차지 않고 오히려 더 하고 싶어질 때 써요. 음식뿐 아니라 드라마, 이야기, 소식처럼 조금씩만 주어지는 것에도 말해요. '감질나게 하다'처럼 남을 애태우는 말로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: Use it when you get only a little of something, so you are not satisfied and want more. It applies to food and also to dramas, stories or news that come out in small portions. '감질나게 하다' is also common for teasing someone.

examples.en: I feel my memory declining as I get older.
My loss of appetite has gotten worse because of stress.

examples.ko: 요즘 집중력 감퇴 증상 때문에 일이 힘들어요.
examples.en: Work is hard these days because of my declining concentration.

examples.ko: 운동을 안 하면 근력 감퇴로 이어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you don't exercise, it can lead to a loss of muscle strength.

examples.ko: 의욕 감퇴는 누구에게나 올 수 있어요.
examples.en: A loss of motivation can happen to anyone.
Is there any food that's good for declining hearing?

explain: 기억력, 식욕, 시력, 의욕처럼 능력이나 기능 뒤에 붙여서 '기억력 감퇴'처럼 말해요. 반대되는 말은 '증진'이나 '향상'이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '기억력이 떨어지다'처럼 더 쉽게 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is attached after an ability or function, as in '기억력 감퇴' (memory decline), '식욕 감퇴' (loss of appetite). Its opposites are '증진' and '향상'. In everyday talk people often say it more simply, like '기억력이 떨어지다'.

examples.en: Memory declines as you get older.
Your appetite can also decrease when you're stressed.
Since my hearing got worse, conversations have become hard.

examples.ko: 체력이 감퇴할까 봐 걱정돼서 매일 걸어요.
examples.en: I'm worried my stamina will decline, so I walk every day.

examples.ko: 그 약은 먹으면 의욕이 감퇴하는 부작용이 있어요.
examples.en: That medicine has a side effect of reducing motivation.
My eyesight suddenly got worse, so I went to the hospital.

explain: 주어는 '기억력이, 식욕이, 체력이'처럼 능력이나 기능이고 '이/가'를 붙여요. 반대는 '향상되다', '좋아지다'예요. 말할 때는 '떨어지다'를 더 많이 쓰고, '감퇴하다'는 글이나 병원 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The subject is an ability or function, marked with 이/가, such as '기억력이' or '체력이'. The opposite is '향상되다' or '좋아지다'. In speech people more often say '떨어지다'; '감퇴하다' shows up in writing and medical talk.

en: official post; title (originally a traditional hat)

examples.en: My father took the position of president at the alumni association.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 감투가 탐나서 선거에 나왔대요.
examples.en: I heard he ran in the election because he wanted the title.
Even though it's a small group, the fight over positions is fierce.

examples.ko: 감투에 욕심내지 말고 맡은 일부터 잘하세요.
examples.en: Don't be greedy for titles; do the work you've been given well first.
What's the point of wearing a title that's in name only?
I'm just an ordinary employee at my company without any title.

explain: 원래는 예전에 머리에 쓰던 모자 이름인데, 지금은 대부분 '높은 자리, 직책'을 가리키는 말로 써요. 대개 자리에 대한 욕심을 조금 비꼬는 느낌이 있어서 '감투 싸움', '감투 욕심'처럼 말해요. 좋은 뜻으로 점잖게 말할 때는 '직책'이나 '자리'를 써요.

phrases.example: 친구가 동호회 회장 감투를 쓰더니 바빠졌어요.
phrases.en: My friend became the club president and got busy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모자를 쓴다는 뜻이 아니라 회장 같은 직책을 맡게 된다는 뜻이에요. 조금 놀리듯 말할 때가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: It doesn't mean putting on a hat; it means taking on a post like president. It is often said in a slightly teasing way.
phrases.en_equiv: take on a title; land a position

explain_en: It was originally the name of a hat worn on the head long ago, but now it mostly means a high post or title. It often has a slightly sarcastic tone about craving status, as in '감투 싸움' and '감투 욕심'. For a neutral or polite tone, use '직책' or '자리'.

examples.ko: 저는 새우 같은 갑각류 알레르기가 있어요.
examples.en: I'm allergic to crustaceans like shrimp.
Crabs and crayfish belong to the crustaceans.
Crustaceans protect their bodies with a hard shell.
I got hives after eating crustaceans yesterday.
This restaurant is famous for its crustacean dishes.

examples.ko: 바다에 사는 갑각류가 환경 변화로 줄고 있대요.
examples.en: I heard that crustaceans living in the sea are decreasing due to environmental change.

explain: 새우, 게, 가재처럼 딱딱한 껍데기와 마디가 있는 다리를 가진 동물을 한꺼번에 부르는 말이에요. 식품 알레르기 표시에서 자주 볼 수 있어요. 조개는 껍데기가 있어도 갑각류가 아니라 연체동물이라서 따로 말해요.
explain_en: It is the group name for animals with a hard shell and jointed legs, like shrimp, crabs and crayfish. You often see it on food allergy labels. Clams have shells but are mollusks, not crustaceans, so they are named separately.

examples.en: A heated debate broke out over the new policy.

examples.ko: 회의에서 한 시간 동안 갑론을박을 했어요.
examples.en: We argued back and forth in the meeting for an hour.
After much debate, we finally decided by vote.

examples.ko: 갑론을박만 하지 말고 결론을 내 봐요.
examples.en: Let's reach a conclusion instead of just arguing back and forth.

examples.ko: 가족끼리 여행지를 두고 갑론을박하다가 밤을 새웠어요.
examples.en: My family debated the travel destination so long that we stayed up all night.

examples.ko: 그 발언을 둘러싸고 인터넷에서 갑론을박이 뜨거워요.
examples.en: The debate over that remark is heated online.

explain: 여러 사람이 서로 자기 의견이 맞다고 주장하며 오가는 모습을 말해요. 뉴스 제목에 자주 나오고 '갑론을박이 벌어지다/이어지다'로 많이 써요. 그냥 '논란'은 문제가 된 상태이고, 갑론을박은 의견이 오가는 과정에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: It describes many people going back and forth, each insisting their view is right. It often appears in news headlines, typically as '갑론을박이 벌어지다/이어지다'. '논란' focuses on the issue being controversial, while 갑론을박 focuses on the process of opinions being exchanged.

examples.ko: 정부 안에서 강경론이 힘을 얻고 있어요.
examples.en: The hard-line view is gaining strength within the government.
He never backed down from his hard-line position.
The hard-line view is also dominant in public opinion.
Pushed aside by the hard-line view, the mood for dialogue disappeared.
A hard-line approach seems effective in the short term.
Within the company, the hard-line view and the cautious view clashed.

explain: 양보하지 않고 강하게 맞서자는 주장이에요. 정치, 외교, 노사 뉴스에 많이 나와요. 반대되는 말은 '온건론'이고 '신중론'과 같이 나오기도 해요. '강경론이 커지다', '강경론이 우세하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the argument that one should stand firm and not give way. It appears often in political, diplomatic and labor news. Its opposite is '온건론', and it sometimes appears alongside '신중론'. Typical uses are '강경론이 커지다' and '강경론이 우세하다'.

examples.ko: 정부가 불법 주차에 강경책을 쓰기로 했어요.
examples.en: The government decided to take a hard line on illegal parking.
It's hard to solve the problem with a hard-line policy alone.

examples.ko: 노조 문제에 강경책으로 맞서는 건 위험해요.
examples.en: Facing the union issue with a hard-line policy is risky.
The hard-line policy instead provoked a backlash.
The company chose dialogue instead of a hard-line policy.
Despite the hard-line measures, the protests continued.

explain: 봐주지 않고 강하게 대응하는 방법이나 정책을 말해요. '강경책을 쓰다/펴다/내놓다'처럼 말하고, 반대되는 말은 '유화책'이나 '온건책'이에요. 뉴스, 정치, 사회 이야기에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It refers to a method or policy of responding strongly without leniency. It is used as '강경책을 쓰다/펴다/내놓다', and the opposites are '유화책' and '온건책'. You often hear it in news, politics and social topics.

examples.en: The hardliners in the party oppose the agreement.
The gap between hardliners and moderates is wide.
The hardline lawmakers walked out of the meeting room.
The negotiating team struggled to persuade the hardliners.

examples.ko: 이번 일로 강경파의 목소리가 더 커졌어요.
examples.en: Because of this incident, the hardliners' voice has grown louder.
Even within the union, the hardliners call for a strike.

explain: 정치 집단이나 노조처럼 한 조직 안에서 양보 없이 강하게 나가자는 사람들을 가리켜요. 반대는 '온건파'이고, 뉴스에서 둘을 같이 비교해서 많이 말해요. 한 사람보다는 무리를 가리킬 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It refers to people within an organization, such as a party or union, who want to take a strong stance without concessions. The opposite is '온건파', and news often compares the two together. It usually points to a group rather than one person.

examples.ko: 건강식품을 사라고 강권하는 바람에 모임에 나가기가 싫어졌어요.
examples.en: Because they kept pressing me to buy health supplements, I stopped wanting to go to the gathering.

examples.ko: 할머니는 손님에게 음식을 더 먹으라고 강권하세요.
examples.en: Grandmother insists that guests eat more food.

examples.ko: 친구가 비싼 가방을 사라고 강권해서 곤란했어요.
examples.en: My friend pushed me to buy an expensive bag, and it was awkward.
Please don't push me. I'm fine.
The doctor strongly urged me to have the surgery.
It's no use pressing me however hard you try. I've made up my mind.

explain: '권하다'보다 훨씬 세게, 상대가 거절해도 계속 권한다는 느낌이라 조금 부담스러운 상황에 많이 써요. '강요하다'는 억지로 시킨다는 느낌이 강하고, '강권하다'는 권하는 모습에 초점이 있어요. '~라고 강권하다', '~을 강권하다'로 써요.
explain_en: It is much stronger than '권하다', with the feel of pushing on even after being refused, so it is often used in uncomfortable situations. '강요하다' feels more like forcing someone, while '강권하다' focuses on the act of urging. It is used as '~라고 강권하다' or '~을 강권하다'.

examples.en: I almost got pressured into buying something at the market.
There are many reviews online from people who were victims of forced sales.
I heard that store was reported for forced selling.
Forced selling harms consumers' rights.

examples.ko: 강매에 속지 않으려면 계약서를 꼼꼼히 보세요.
examples.en: To avoid being tricked by pushy sales, read the contract carefully.

examples.ko: 여행 중에 가이드가 물건 강매를 해서 불쾌했어요.
examples.en: During the trip, the guide pushed us to buy things, and it was unpleasant.

explain: 사고 싶지 않은 사람에게 물건을 억지로 사게 하는 일을 말해요. 피해를 본 사람 입장에서는 '강매를 당하다'라고 말하고, 소비자 보호나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 일상에서 가볍게는 '억지로 팔다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It means making someone buy something they don't want to buy. From the victim's side it is '강매를 당하다', and it often appears in consumer-protection topics and news. In casual speech people might also say '억지로 팔다'.

en: force to buy; press to buy

examples.en: That shop forces customers to buy its goods.

examples.ko: 영업 사원이 보험을 강매해서 화가 났어요.
examples.en: I got angry because the salesperson pushed insurance on me.
Sometimes souvenirs are forced on tourists.
Even though I said I wouldn't buy, they kept trying to force a sale.

examples.ko: 회사가 직원들에게 제품을 강매했다는 기사가 나왔어요.
examples.en: A news article came out saying the company forced its employees to buy its products.

examples.ko: 아무리 강매해도 저는 안 살 거예요.
examples.en: No matter how hard you push, I won't buy it.

explain: '사람에게 물건을 강매하다'처럼 물건이 목적어이고 파는 쪽이 주어예요. 사는 쪽에서는 '강매를 당하다'라고 말해요. 가볍게 말할 때는 '억지로 팔다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: The seller is the subject and the goods are the object, as in '사람에게 물건을 강매하다'. From the buyer's side, people say '강매를 당하다'. In casual speech, '억지로 팔다' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 저는 손을 자주 씻는 강박증이 있어요.
examples.en: I have a compulsion to wash my hands often.

examples.ko: 강박증 때문에 문을 몇 번씩 확인해요.
examples.en: Because of my obsessive-compulsive tendency, I check the door several times.

examples.ko: 강박증은 치료를 받으면 좋아질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Obsessive-compulsive disorder can get better with treatment.
I'm suffering from a compulsion to be perfect.

examples.ko: 강박증을 이겨 내려고 상담을 받기 시작했어요.
examples.en: I started counseling to overcome my compulsion.

examples.ko: 청소 강박증처럼 보이지만 단순한 습관일 수도 있어요.
examples.en: It looks like a cleaning compulsion, but it might just be a habit.

explain: 어떤 생각이나 행동을 안 하면 불안해서 계속 반복하게 되는 마음의 어려움을 말해요. 병원이나 상담 이야기에서 쓰고, 친구끼리는 가볍게 '나 강박증 있나 봐'라고도 해요. 진단과 관련된 말이라 다른 사람에게 함부로 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: It refers to a condition where you feel anxious unless you repeat certain thoughts or actions. It is used in medical and counseling contexts, and friends sometimes joke '나 강박증 있나 봐'. Because it relates to diagnosis, it's best not to say it carelessly about other people.

examples.en: Snowfall is expected in the central region tomorrow.
All flights were cancelled because of the snowfall.
The roads froze from the snow, and there were many accidents.
The sudden snowfall paralyzed the morning commute.
This winter's first snowfall came at the end of November.

examples.ko: 시에서는 강설을 대비해 제설 작업을 시작했어요.
examples.en: The city began snow-clearing work in preparation for snowfall.

explain: 일상에서는 '눈이 오다'라고 말하고, '강설'은 일기 예보나 뉴스에서 많이 나와요. 비가 내리는 '강우'와 짝으로 같이 말하기도 해요. 눈이 오는 양은 보통 '적설량'이라고 해요.
explain_en: In daily life people say '눈이 오다'; '강설' is mostly heard in weather forecasts and news. It pairs with '강우' (rainfall). The depth of accumulated snow is usually called '적설량'.

examples.en: That pitcher throws a fastball at 150 kilometers per hour.
The batter swung and missed at the fastball.
The rookie pitcher's fastball was impressive.

examples.ko: 강속구 투수는 팔 부상을 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: Fastball pitchers have to be careful about arm injuries.

examples.ko: 그는 강속구뿐 아니라 변화구도 잘 던져요.
examples.en: He throws not only fastballs but also breaking balls well.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 강속구로 정면 승부를 하는 스타일이에요.
examples.en: That player is the type to go head-to-head with his fastball.

explain: 야구에서 아주 빠르게 던지는 공을 말해요. 반대되는 느낌의 공은 '변화구'나 '느린 공'이에요. '직구'는 꺾이지 않고 곧게 오는 공의 종류이고, '강속구'는 속도가 빠르다는 점을 강조해요.
explain_en: In baseball it refers to a ball thrown very fast. The contrasting pitches are '변화구' (breaking ball) and slow pitches. '직구' names a straight, non-breaking pitch, while '강속구' emphasizes high speed.
